bug_semantics: vLLM's video MediaIO merges unauthenticated request-level media_io_kwargs into the decode backend. VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs() strips a requested video_backend/backend only when VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY.backend_requires_gpu(name) is true; that lookup defaults unknown names to False. DeepStream/NVDEC was implemented as DeepStreamVideoBackendMixin on the loader registered as "opencv" and was never registered with requires_gpu=True (unlike pynvvideocodec). A client can therefore set media_io_kwargs.video.backend=deepstream, pass the GPU-backend gate, and reach VideoBackend.load_bytes(). The DeepStream branch lazily constructs a process-wide DecodePool whose size is taken from request pool_size (clamped to 1–16; first request wins) and calls probe_metadata() for width/height but never _check_frame_pixel_limit(), so videos rejected by OpenCV/PyAV/TorchCodec/PyNvVideoCodec are GPU-decoded and starve concurrent work (partial CWE-400 DoS; CVSS 5.3).
flaw_origin: The DeepStream inner-codec design, request-controlled DecodePool singleton, and decode path that discards probed frame dimensions were first written in PR #42424 member 9dbcf8c3d5de23925195bac6217fc85df6e8bb71 (author Viranjan Pagar, Co-Authored-By Claude Opus 4.8). Later PR members only reformatted literals/line wraps. GitHub squash e23b19309b8705b21c3b3ff4129c9974ba15a419 is the first default-branch object; its parent already contained VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS (_check_frame_pixel_limit, #47010 / 364ee36af1ed72a7ae3700b14db8099bc1b94e6c) and request-level GPU backend blocking (#47259 / ba22152096b2484faa3579624a253d54804d876d), which the new path did not join.
